propositions: Operators lack an on-demand, non-blocking way to verify that mapped project keys and legacy_default in projects.json are actually visible to the bot outside a full reconcile pass.

The bridge fsck command must gain an opt-in --live-visibility flag that performs a live mapped-key visibility check by reusing the shared helper from ticket D, gated by credential presence (JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, JIRA_API_TOKEN).

When credentials are present, the new fsck step calls check_mapped_project_visibility() and reports each mapped key's visibility status to stderr; when credentials are absent and no probe is injected, the step emits an advisory skipped verdict without calling the probe.
The new --live-visibility step must not alter the default bridge fsck exit contract, must not mutate bridge state, and must not add fields to the stdout JSON output (verdict goes to stderr only).
Core rebar doctor must remain Jira-free with no new reconciler or agents imports reachable from _commands/doctor.py.
The shared visibility helper from ticket D must be the single source of truth for mapped-project existence checks; no duplicate Jira existence check logic.
